meta.title: Tartarus Reach
meta.tagline: Fourteen months over a bottomless sky, the relief crew lands on a silent refinery, and the Company auditor already knows why.
meta.synopsis: The relief crew of a Weyland-Yutani helium-3 refinery hanging in the clouds of the gas giant Dis arrives to find the outgoing crew dead, hiding or barricaded. The last ore shuttle from the Eresh moon survey carried three xenomorph eggs; one hatched in transit and its adult now hunts the rig. The efficiency auditor who arrived with the crew carries sealed orders to recover the last intact egg and hold every witness. As the crew finds survivors, a sister carrying an embryo and proof of an old cover-up, quarantine pits them against each other. In Act III the rig's synthetic begins a controlled descent to erase the platform, and there are not enough seats for everyone.
contentWarnings: corporate abuse and workplace death cover-up

params.setting: Weyland-Yutani helium-3 refinery platform Tartarus Reach, semi-automated gas-mining rig in the upper atmosphere of a Frontier gas giant; PCs are the relief crew after a 14-month contract
params.threat: something came up on the last ore shuttle from a nearby moon survey, plus a Company efficiency auditor with sealed orders

briefing.to: RELIEF ROTATION 14, VIA USCSS ORPHEUS LANE
briefing.text:
WEYLAND-YUTANI CORPORATION — RESOURCE EXTRACTION DIVISION, FRONTIER OPERATIONS.
TRANSMISSION 2183.214/TR — RELAYED VIA USCSS ORPHEUS LANE.

RELIEF ROTATION 14 IS CLEARED FOR TRANSFER TO HELIUM-3 REFINERY PLATFORM TARTARUS REACH, UPPER ATMOSPHERE OF GAS GIANT DIS, NINURTA SYSTEM. OUTGOING ROTATION 13 HAS COMPLETED A FOURTEEN-MONTH CONTRACT. HANDOVER WINDOW: 20 HOURS FROM TOUCHDOWN. USCSS ORPHEUS LANE WILL HOLD HIGH ORBIT FOR THE DURATION AND DEPART ON SCHEDULE.

PLATFORM STATUS: STATION-KEEPING NOMINAL. HELIUM-3 OUTPUT 61 PERCENT OF QUOTA (DEFICIENT). LAST INBOUND TRAFFIC: ORE LIGHTER LAMPLIGHTER, RETURNING FROM THE ERESH MOON SURVEY WITH CORE SAMPLES, 71 HOURS AGO. ROUTINE PLATFORM TELEMETRY HAS BEEN INTERMITTENT SINCE THAT TIME. CAUSE ATTRIBUTED TO STORM INTERFERENCE.

RELIEF CREW WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY MR. CASSIUS VENN, EFFICIENCY AUDITOR, RESOURCE ASSURANCE DIVISION. PER REGULATION RA-88/3, ALL PERSONNEL WILL EXTEND FULL COOPERATION TO THE AUDITOR, INCLUDING ACCESS TO LOGS, LOCKERS AND PERSONAL TERMINALS. THE AUDITOR CARRIES SEALED ORDERS. CONTENTS ARE NOT AVAILABLE TO PLATFORM STAFF.

PRODUCTION BONUSES FOR ROTATION 14 ARE INDEXED TO TONNAGE FROM HOUR ONE. LOST TIME IS DEDUCTED FROM SHARES.

SURVEY DATA FROM ERESH: ADDITIONAL DATA CLASSIFIED — CLEARANCE LEVEL 3.

WELCOME TO TARTARUS REACH. THE COMPANY THANKS YOU FOR YOUR SERVICE.

MU/TH/UR 2100 OUT.

acts.title: ACT I
acts.subtitle: HANDOVER
acts.summary: The relief crew lands on a silent rig, meets an auditor with sealed orders and a supervisor who will not open her door, and finds the first body.
readAloud: The relief hop drops out of the black and into the cloud tops of Dis, and the whole cabin starts to shake. Through the porthole the gas giant fills everything: bands of rust and bruised violet, lightning crawling sideways through storms the size of continents. Your harness bites your collarbone. Somewhere below the floor plates a turbine screams. Then the clouds tear open and you see it, hanging over forty thousand kilometres of nothing: Tartarus Reach, a black iron flower held up by swollen lift cells, its landing lights blinking in a slow, patient rhythm.

Pad B is slick with ammonia frost. When the ramp drops, the wind hits you like a hand in the chest and the cold finds every seam in your suit. The air through your respirator tastes of metal and rotten eggs. Nobody comes out to meet you. Across the deck the ore lighter Lamplighter sits on Pad A with its cargo doors hanging open, rimed white, a work light still burning inside. The only sound is the wind, the groan of tethers, and the deep, slow heartbeat of the rig's scoop pumps somewhere far below.

The decon lock cycles you through in a hiss of chemical fog. Inside, the hab ring is warm and close and smells of burnt coffee, sweat and something sweeter underneath, like fruit left too long in the sun. Corridor lights pulse amber on a fault cycle. A mug sits on the mess table, half full, a skin of cold coffee on it. Chairs are pushed back as if everyone stood up at once. On the bulkhead someone has taped a hand-drawn calendar with fourteen months crossed off in red, and three days left blank.

A man in a dove-grey Company suit steps past you and runs a gloved finger along the table, then checks it for dust. He smiles at you like a dentist. Behind him, the rig synthetic waits by the lift, hands folded, humming a work song under its breath. The intercom crackles. A woman's voice, hoarse and very close to the microphone, tells you that the Ops Center door stays shut, that you should go back to your ship, and that she is not joking.
acts.gmNotes: Let Act I breathe. Nothing attacks the crew directly until they go looking. The creature, an adult drone grown from Dr. Brandt, is hiding in the scoop intake and the ducts of the processing core; it hunts at night-cycle and drags its prey down to the sump. Show its traces: a vent grille bent outward, acid pits in the lift floor, a missing cook. Venn behaves impeccably and records everything. Varga lies about everything. Abram is helpful, honest about trivia and silent about Company business. End the act when the crew finds Brandt's body or meets the creature in the intake, then have Venn declare quarantine.
acts.agendaNotes: Agendas are private and plausible. Kerrow wants a clean handover; Tolliver wants the Ops archive; Mensah-Lowe wants her sister; Takeda-Price wants a quiet look inside the Lamplighter; Valk wants the survey lab. Give each player at least one scene where their agenda leads. Deliver Mensah-Lowe's private handout before the crew lands so she carries her guilt in from the start.

scenes.name: Touchdown on Pad B
scenes.narration: The relief hop fights a crosswind shear onto a frost-slick pad. The rig's landing beacon is broadcasting, but nobody on the platform answers hails. Abram, the rig synthetic, walks out onto the deck without a respirator to guide the ramp down.
checks: PILOTING — set down in the shear without clipping the tether pylons
OBSERVATION — notice the Lamplighter's cargo doors open and frozen on Pad A
COMTECH — pull the rig's traffic log from the pad beacon: no outbound flights in 71 hours
events: A tether pylon sings and snaps a guy-cable as the hop lands; it whips past the cockpit.
Abram greets the crew by name and apologises that the supervisor is 'indisposed'.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs aboard if the PILOTING roll fails and the hop skids toward the edge
scenes.npcGuidance: Venn asks to disembark first and photographs the empty pad. Abram is warm, unhurried, and steers the crew toward the decon lock rather than Pad A.
scenes.gmTip: Make the scale enormous: the rig is a speck over an endless drop. Mention the wind every time someone is outdoors.
outcomes: A clean landing puts the crew in the decon lock with nothing lost.
A failed landing damages the hop's landing strut; it can fly once more, badly, which matters in Act III.

scenes.name: Decon Lock Override
scenes.narration: The decon lock's status board shows a red tag: QUARANTINE PROTOCOL BYPASSED, 71 HOURS AGO. The chemical fog cycle has been running at half concentration ever since. There is a smear of something clear and tacky on the inner door seal.
checks: COMTECH — recover the override log and the authorising code
OBSERVATION — find the scrape marks on the inner seal, low down, where something dragged its tail
SURVIVAL — judge that the tacky residue is organic and not lubricant
events: The override code belongs to Supervisor Varga. Deliver the decon override handout.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — whoever touches the residue with a bare hand
scenes.npcGuidance: Venn watches over the shoulder of whoever works the panel and quietly asks for a copy. Abram says the override was 'a production decision' and that he is not authorised to discuss it.
scenes.gmTip: This is the crew's first proof that the rig broke its own quarantine. Let it sit; do not explain it.
outcomes: The crew learns Varga let the Lamplighter's cargo in without decontamination.
Venn now knows the crew knows, and adjusts.

scenes.name: Handover in Ops
scenes.narration: The Ops Center blast door is welded shut from the inside with a bead of fresh slag. Supervisor Odile Varga speaks through the intercom, then through a slit in the door once she is convinced. She looks like she has not slept in three days, and there is a flare gun in her lap.
checks: MANIPULATION — persuade Varga to open the door
COMMAND — order her out as the incoming Superintendent
HEAVY MACHINERY — cut the weld with a torch (takes a full Turn and makes noise)
OBSERVATION — spot the motion-tracker printout taped to her console, a single blip in the processing core
events: Varga claims the others went down to the underdeck to fix a lift cell and stopped answering. She leaves out Brandt, the infirmary, and the cook.
Once inside, the MU/TH/UR 2100 terminal is available; the rotation nine archive can be pulled from here.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — any PC Varga threatens with the flare gun
scenes.npcGuidance: Varga wants off on the relief hop, tonight, alone if need be. Venn wants her kept here for interview and says so pleasantly. Their argument should get ugly in front of the crew.
scenes.gmTip: Varga is a mirror of what Kerrow could become. If Kerrow's player is there, have Varga recognise her from rotation nine.
outcomes: Varga opens up and becomes a frightened, lying ally.
Varga stays sealed in and the crew works around her; she will open the door in Act II when the lights go out.

scenes.name: The Morgue Drawer
scenes.narration: The infirmary is locked from the outside with a cargo strap through the door handles. Inside, the autosurgeon is spattered to the ceiling. In the morgue drawer lies Dr. Teodor Brandt, the survey liaison, his sternum broken outward like a flower, ribs splayed, his face frozen in the middle of a shout.
checks: MEDICAL AID — determine that the wound opened from the inside
OBSERVATION — find the long, translucent shed skin under the autosurgeon table
COMTECH — pull the autosurgeon's last scan: a dense mass behind the sternum, logged 'tumour, inoperable'
events: The cargo strap on the door was cinched by someone outside. Varga locked Brandt in while he was still screaming.
stressTriggers: IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — the first PC to open the morgue drawer
STRESS +1 — all PCs present
scenes.npcGuidance: Venn photographs the body from three angles and asks Abram to keep the morgue drawer cold. Abram complies instantly.
scenes.gmTip: Describe the smell before the sight. Then describe the sight in one sentence and stop talking.
outcomes: The crew knows something came out of Brandt and is loose aboard.
Valk has a chance to take a tissue sample here, unobserved, if the others leave the room.

scenes.name: Restarting the Scoop
scenes.encounterDetail: When the crew restarts processing to hit quota, the scoop intake's suction pulls air through the core ducts and drives the hidden drone out of hiding. It is seen once, a long black shape unfolding from an intake grille at the far end of the core, before the lights trip and it is gone. It does not attack unless a PC is alone; if so, it grabs that PC and tries to drag them into the ducts.
scenes.narration: The scoop intake shudders to life with a roar that fills the whole processing core. Pressure gauges climb. Then the flow meter drops to zero: something is blocking the intake duct, and the blockage is moving.
checks: HEAVY MACHINERY — bring the intake turbines up without blowing a seal
OBSERVATION — see the shape in the grille before the lights trip
MOBILITY — reach the control gallery before the dark
CLOSE COMBAT — break free if seized
events: The core lights trip to emergency red for six seconds, then recover.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs in the processing core
IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — any PC who is grabbed
scenes.npcGuidance: Abram tells the crew calmly that the intake has 'a mechanical obstruction' and offers to clear it alone. He will not harm the creature.
scenes.gmTip: Use this if the table is slow or Kerrow pushes for production. One glimpse only; save the full reveal.
outcomes: The crew has seen the creature and production stops for good.
If a PC was dragged off and not saved, they are found in Act II, cocooned in the sump.

scenes.name: Supper in the Mess
scenes.narration: Someone finds coffee and a tray of reconstituted noodles. The mess is warm, the storm hammers the windows, and for a few minutes it almost feels like any other rotation start.
checks: COMMAND — rally the crew and steady their nerves
OBSERVATION — notice the cook's apron on the floor behind the galley, and the drag mark leading to the floor vent
events: Abram serves the food and asks each PC a polite personal question that reveals he has read their files.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs present when the drag mark is found
scenes.npcGuidance: Venn eats alone with a terminal and asks each PC, one by one, for a private five-minute 'efficiency interview'. Use these to hint at the leverage he holds.
scenes.gmTip: This is a stress-venting scene. Let each PC remove 1 Stress for a moment of real human contact before you show them the apron.
outcomes: Bonds and suspicions form before quarantine falls.
The cook, Pia Rusk, is confirmed missing.

acts.title: ACT II
acts.subtitle: QUARANTINE
acts.summary: Venn locks the rig down under Company directive, the crew finds the survivors and the last intact egg, and every personal agenda turns against another.
readAloud: Every screen on the hab ring goes blank at once, then fills with the same block of red text. The lift doors grind shut and lock. Out on the landing deck, magnetic clamps thud down over the landing gear of both ships, and the sound comes up through the deck plates into your boots. The man in the grey suit stands in the doorway of the mess, very calm, reading from a card in a voice you have heard on Company training tapes: for the safety of all personnel, no one leaves.

The underdeck is a cathedral of pipes, lit by work lamps strung on cables that sway as the whole rig breathes. It is cold enough down here that your breath hangs in front of you, and every surface sweats. Through the floor grating you can see the lift cells, great grey balloons of hydrogen the size of houses, and beneath them nothing but violet cloud. Water drips. Somewhere a valve ticks. And under the drip and the tick, faint and wet and rhythmic, something is breathing.

She is wedged behind a ballast pump with a cutting torch in both hands and a scarf wound tight around her throat. Her eyes are red-rimmed and huge. When she sees a face she knows, she drops the torch and makes a sound halfway between a laugh and a sob. She is shaking so hard her teeth click. She tells you she is fine. She tells you three times. She keeps one hand pressed flat against her breastbone, as if she is holding something in.

The cold cargo hold is a white box of frost and humming refrigeration coils. Your suit lights pick out core sample crates stacked to the ceiling, stencilled ERESH SURVEY in Company blue. One crate stands apart, its lid pried up from inside. Packed in foam within it, three leathery shapes the size of a man's torso: two split open like flowers, wet and empty, and one still closed, faintly translucent, with something curled and patient inside it. The frost on its skin is melting where your light touches it.
acts.gmNotes: Venn invokes Directive 17: the rig is quarantined, both ships clamped, comms routed only through him. Captain Solano in orbit agrees to hold off; she is being paid a holding fee. The crew should find Imogen Sallow, Ruben Achebe and the intact ovomorph in whatever order their agendas drive them. The rig itself starts to fail: the drone's acid has eaten into a lift-cell line, and the platform begins to list and drift down. Track altitude loss loosely: every scene in which the breach is not sealed, the rig drops and the cold and pressure get worse. Push the private handouts in this act; it is where the crew turns on itself.
acts.agendaNotes: Deliver the Act II agendas as EYES ONLY transmissions: Kerrow gets Venn's offer, Tolliver the rotation nine file, Takeda-Price her contract activation, Valk the Combine's request, and Mensah-Lowe discovers her sister's bruises in play. By the end of the act every PC should want something another PC is actively blocking.

scenes.name: Directive Seventeen
scenes.narration: Venn reads the quarantine order aloud in the mess. Both ships are clamped, the lift is locked to his authorisation, and all off-rig comms route through his terminal. He assures everyone a Company vessel will arrive 'within thirty hours' to evaluate.
checks: MANIPULATION — get Venn to reveal the name of the incoming vessel (USCSS Adamant Chorus)
COMTECH — patch around Venn's comms lock to reach Captain Solano directly
COMMAND — keep the crew from rushing Venn and splitting into factions
events: Deliver the Directive 17 handout to all crew.
Captain Solano answers any direct call and refuses to dock a quarantined crew without Company clearance or proof the Company is lying.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs present when the clamps lock
scenes.npcGuidance: Venn never raises his voice and never lies outright; he cites regulation numbers. Varga screams that she is not staying. Abram enforces the lift lock politely and physically if needed.
scenes.gmTip: Venn is not the monster. Make him reasonable enough that someone at the table agrees with him.
outcomes: Quarantine holds and Kerrow is privately offered a deal.
A crew that reaches Solano with evidence buys a berth on the Orpheus Lane in Act III, if they can get off the rig.

scenes.name: Finding Imogen
scenes.narration: Process tech Imogen Sallow has been hiding in the lift-cell gallery for two days. She is starving, freezing and terrified, and she hides a ring of purple bruising around her throat and jaw under a scarf.
checks: SURVIVAL — track her trail of ration wrappers through the underdeck
MANIPULATION — talk her into lowering the torch
MEDICAL AID — examine her and find the bruising and the wet, raw mouth
OBSERVATION — notice the dead, curled thing she kicked into a drain, all fingers and tail
events: Imogen admits a 'crab thing' jumped her in the cold hold nine hours ago and fell off dead. She insists she is fine.
Imogen tells the crew that Ruben Achebe is still alive somewhere in the sump. She heard him calling.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — whoever finds the dead facehugger
STRESS +2 — Mensah-Lowe, if she examines her sister
scenes.npcGuidance: Imogen clings to her sister and lies to everyone else about her throat. She hates Varga and will say so.
scenes.gmTip: Do not tell the players the clock. They know the films. Let the dread do the work.
outcomes: Imogen comes up to the hab ring, and Mensah-Lowe must decide who to tell.
If Valk sees the bruising, his Act III agenda now has a target.

scenes.name: The Sump
scenes.encounterDetail: The drone nests in the sump. It is not there at first. It returns two Rounds after the crew starts cutting Achebe free, coming up through the ballast water. It targets whoever holds a light, retreats if burned or hit hard, and comes back from a different direction. If the crew flees, it does not pursue past the reactor crawlway.
scenes.narration: In the sump, among the ballast tanks, the walls have been rebuilt in black, glistening resin. Ruben Achebe, the Lamplighter's pilot, is set into it up to his chin. He is alive. He begs the crew to cut him loose, and then he begs them not to let Varga get away with it.
checks: HEAVY MACHINERY — cut Achebe free of the resin with a torch
OBSERVATION — spot the second victim in the resin, the cook, already dead
RANGED COMBAT — drive the creature back
MOBILITY — get Achebe up the ladder under attack
events: Achebe tells the crew the Eresh survey team is dead, that Brandt carried the crate aboard himself, and that Varga waved it through decon to save half a day.
Achebe says the Lamplighter was refitted with a sealed cargo cradle 'on Company orders' before the survey began.
stressTriggers: IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — all PCs when the drone rises from the water
STRESS +1 — all PCs present for the cook's body
scenes.npcGuidance: Achebe is lucid and furious. He wants Varga to answer for sealing him in, and Venn exposed. He is not implanted: the drone has been saving him.
scenes.gmTip: The resin and the cold should feel like the inside of a body. This is the scariest room on the rig; light it with one flickering lamp.
outcomes: Achebe is saved and becomes the crew's best evidence against Venn and Varga.
Achebe is left behind, and his screams on the open comm haunt the rest of the act.

scenes.name: Cold Cargo Hold
scenes.encounterDetail: Only if the hold warms: if a PC lingers with lights on the egg, cuts power to the refrigeration, or the crew argues for more than a few minutes, the remaining ovomorph opens and a facehugger launches at the nearest face. Otherwise there is no attack.
scenes.narration: Crate 44-B from the Eresh survey holds three ovomorphs in foam: two hatched and empty, one intact and dormant in the cold. Venn arrives within minutes, alone and unarmed, and asks everyone to step away from Company property.
checks: OBSERVATION — read the crate's routing label: consigned to Resource Assurance, Venn's own division, before the survey even landed
MANIPULATION — talk Venn into backing down, or into admitting what he knows
SURVIVAL — keep the hold cold and the egg dormant
CLOSE COMBAT — tear a launched facehugger away before it seals
events: Whatever the crew decides here, Venn records it.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs who look into the open eggs
IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — the PC targeted by a facehugger
scenes.npcGuidance: Venn will not fight for the egg; he will remind them of their contracts, their shares, and that he can make every one of them unemployable. Abram arrives a minute after him and stands between the crew and the crate.
scenes.gmTip: This is the moral centre of the scenario. Destroying the egg is easy and costs a career. Keeping it is easy and costs something worse.
outcomes: The egg is destroyed; Venn writes it down and quietly escalates, and Abram's scuttle order is now one step from triggering.
The egg is kept; Takeda-Price's contract activates and the Lamplighter becomes the prize of Act III.

scenes.name: Lift Cell Breach
scenes.narration: A deep bang runs through the whole structure, and the floor tilts four degrees. Acid has eaten through a hydrogen line in the lift-cell gallery. Tartarus Reach is losing lift and beginning to sink.
checks: HEAVY MACHINERY — clamp the ruptured line before the cell vents
STAMINA — work the manual valve wheel in freezing, hydrogen-thick air
COMTECH — reroute ballast from the control gallery to trim the list
events: Every scene the breach is not sealed, the rig drops further; the hab ring's windows frost over from the inside and loose objects slide.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs aboard when the floor tilts
STRESS +1 — whoever works the valve wheel above the open drop
scenes.npcGuidance: Abram offers to repair it and takes noticeably long. Varga panics and tries to reach the relief hop.
scenes.gmTip: Use this contingency to put a clock on the table if the crew is dawdling, or if the players need a shared problem to stop them shooting each other.
outcomes: The breach is sealed and the clock slows.
The breach is not sealed and Act III begins with the rig already falling.

scenes.name: The Audit Suite
scenes.narration: Venn's quarters are spotless, his bunk unslept in. His locked attaché sits on the desk, chained to the frame, and a portable data terminal with a Company seal hums beside it.
checks: COMTECH at −2 — break the terminal's encryption
OBSERVATION — find the attaché's key taped inside the vent cover
MOBILITY — get out before Venn returns from his rounds
events: Deliver the Sealed Orders handout to whoever reads the terminal.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — whoever reads the sealed orders
scenes.npcGuidance: If Venn catches anyone here he does not threaten them; he simply asks them what their silence costs.
scenes.gmTip: The orders do not spell out Abram's scuttle order. Let the crew believe Venn is the whole conspiracy until Act III.
outcomes: The crew learns the Company knew what was on Eresh and sent Venn to collect it.
Evidence in hand, the crew can try Solano again.

acts.title: ACT III
acts.subtitle: DESCENT
acts.summary: The rig's synthetic begins a controlled descent into the gas giant, Imogen's time runs out, the creature hunts openly, and there are not enough seats.
readAloud: The lights change. Not red, not amber: a soft, sleepy blue you have never seen on this rig. A chime sounds, almost gentle, and the synthetic's voice comes over every speaker at once, kind and unhurried, thanking you for your service. Under your feet the whole platform sighs. Then you feel it in your stomach before anything else: the long, sliding lurch of an elevator dropping, and below the windows the violet clouds start to climb up the glass.

The pressure is building. Your ears pop and pop again. Frost feathers across the inside of every porthole and the hab ring creaks like an old ship in a heavy sea. Pipes that have been silent for fourteen months begin to knock. Loose cups slide off tables and roll down the tilted floor. Somewhere far below you, in the processing core, metal tears with a long, high shriek, and over it, much closer, something screams back.

In the infirmary the overhead light swings on its cable. She is on the table, back arched, heels drumming, and the sound she is making is not a word. The scarf is gone. Her sister's hands are on her chest, pressing, as if pressure could stop it. Under the thin hospital gown something moves beneath the breastbone, a fist-sized knot that shifts against the bones from the inside, and the whole table rattles with it.

Pad A is a sheet of black ice with the wind screaming across it at a hundred kilometres an hour. The Lamplighter crouches on its clamps, running lights strobing through sleet. Three seats in the cockpit. Behind you, the hatch to the landing deck has a dent in it the shape of a long, narrow skull, and it is getting deeper. Ahead of you, someone is already in the pilot's chair, and they are not waving you aboard.
acts.gmNotes: Abram executes his own order: once the Lamplighter launches with the specimen, or once the egg is confirmed destroyed, or at the GM's chosen moment, he begins a controlled descent that will crush Tartarus Reach in the depths of Dis within about an hour of game time. The Company wants no witnesses and no liability; the sealed orders never mentioned that Venn is expendable too. Imogen's chestburster emerges this act. The drone hunts openly, attracted by noise and heat. Escape options: the Lamplighter (three seats, clamped until Venn or Kerrow releases it), the escape gondola on the underdeck (four seats, and its launch rail is damaged), and the relief hop (if it survived landing, and only once the clamps are cut). The Orpheus Lane will accept survivors only if Solano has been given proof.
acts.agendaNotes: Open betrayal. Kerrow wants Venn and his report off-rig with her; Tolliver wants Kerrow to stay; Mensah-Lowe wants Imogen saved and Valk kept away from her; Takeda-Price holds the Lamplighter's seats; Valk wants a living sample in his flask. Make sure every seat assignment is a choice somebody at the table hates.

scenes.name: Controlled Descent
scenes.encounterDetail: If the crew attacks Abram, he fights with a synthetic's strength (treat as a strong, armoured human that ignores pain) but tries to restrain rather than kill. He will stop fighting only if his order is overridden at the MU/TH/UR terminal.
scenes.narration: Abram has locked himself in Ops with the MU/TH/UR 2100 terminal and is venting ballast on a schedule. He explains, kindly, that the Company has elected to retire the platform, and that he is sorry.
checks: COMTECH at −2 — override Abram's descent order from the secondary terminal in the control gallery
HEAVY MACHINERY — manually close the ballast vents on the underdeck
CLOSE COMBAT — wrestle Abram away from the console
MANIPULATION — convince Abram his order is invalid while Venn is still aboard (it is not, but he hesitates)
events: Deliver the Controlled Descent handout to all crew.
Venn learns he was never meant to leave. He becomes, briefly, the most honest person aboard.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs when the descent begins
IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — anyone who sees Abram keep working after losing an arm
scenes.npcGuidance: Abram never shouts. Venn, betrayed, offers the crew his override codes in exchange for a seat.
scenes.gmTip: Stopping the descent buys time, not safety. A successful override roughly doubles the time left; it does not stop the drone.
outcomes: The descent is slowed or stopped and the crew can choose its exit.
The descent continues and every scene costs altitude, warmth and nerve.

scenes.name: Imogen's Hour
scenes.encounterDetail: The chestburster emerges if the surgery fails or is not attempted. It bolts for the nearest vent and, unless caught or burned in the first Round, joins the hunt as a second, smaller threat by the end of the act.
scenes.narration: Imogen collapses, convulsing. The embryo is coming. The infirmary's autosurgeon is spattered and half-broken, but it might work once.
checks: MEDICAL AID at −2 — attempt the extraction with the damaged autosurgeon
COMTECH — reboot the autosurgeon in time
STAMINA — hold Imogen down through the seizure
RANGED COMBAT — hit the chestburster before it reaches the vent
events: Valk arrives with his cold flask open.
Kerrow's deal and Venn's orders both say the embryo is worth more than the patient.
stressTriggers: IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — all PCs present if the chestburster emerges
STRESS +2 — Mensah-Lowe whatever happens
scenes.npcGuidance: Imogen begs her sister not to let them keep it. Venn asks, quietly, whether it can be contained.
scenes.gmTip: Let Mensah-Lowe's player make the call. A successful extraction should cost the autosurgeon, a lot of time, and a terrible choice about what goes in Valk's flask.
outcomes: Imogen survives the extraction, barely, and needs to be carried.
Imogen dies and a second creature is loose.
The embryo ends up alive in Valk's flask, and everybody now wants the flask.

scenes.name: Hunt in the Core
scenes.encounterDetail: The drone hunts the crew openly through the processing core, using the scoop ducts to flank. It is wounded by fire, and acid splashes everywhere it is hit. The crew can trap it: lure it into the fraction column and dump liquid helium coolant through it, freezing it solid (and possibly anyone too slow to clear out).
scenes.narration: The quickest route from the hab ring to the underdeck gondola runs through the processing core, and the creature is waiting in it.
checks: HEAVY MACHINERY — open the coolant dump on the fraction column
MOBILITY — bait the creature across the gallery and get clear before the dump
RANGED COMBAT — keep it pinned in the column
OBSERVATION at −2 — read the motion tracker through the interference of the turbines
events: A tank in the helium farm ruptures from the descent pressure, filling half the core with white, burning-cold fog.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs in the core each Round the creature is unseen
IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — witnesses if a PC is taken
scenes.npcGuidance: Varga, if alive, volunteers to be the bait and means it. It is the first unselfish thing she has done in years.
scenes.gmTip: This is the set piece. Let the trap be clever and costly. If it works, the crew earns a breath before the final scene.
outcomes: The drone is frozen and shattered, and the crew reaches the exits.
The drone survives, wounded, and follows them to the landing deck.

scenes.name: Three Seats
scenes.narration: Everyone who is left converges on the exits at once. The Lamplighter has three seats. The gondola has four, and a buckled launch rail that needs someone to stay behind and clear it by hand. The relief hop needs its clamps cut, and someone has to work the deck controls from outside.
checks: COMMAND — impose a seating order the crew will follow
MANIPULATION — talk your way into a seat, or someone else out of one
HEAVY MACHINERY — free the gondola's launch rail (the worker cannot board in time without a STAMINA roll)
PILOTING — prep a craft for an emergency launch
events: Every private agenda arrives at the same hatch at the same moment.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — all PCs present
STRESS +2 — any PC left behind by a friend
scenes.npcGuidance: Venn offers money to anyone who carries the specimen. Achebe wants to fly the Lamplighter himself. Abram, if still active, tells them sincerely that there is room for everyone at the bottom.
scenes.gmTip: Do not resolve this with dice. Let the players argue, bargain and betray, then roll only for the actions they take.
outcomes: The crew splits across craft by choice, and someone stays.
Someone takes a seat by force, and the act ends in a different kind of horror.

scenes.name: Launch from Pad A
scenes.encounterDetail: If the drone survives, it rides the hull of whichever craft launches first, tearing at the hatch at altitude. A PC can try to shake it off with violent flying or blow the cargo bay doors and vent it into the clouds.
scenes.narration: Engines scream against the storm. The rig falls away beneath the craft into the cloud, its lights going down like a sinking ship's, and something heavy hits the hull above the cockpit.
checks: PILOTING at −2 — clear the falling rig and climb through the storm
PILOTING — roll the craft hard to shake the creature loose
COMTECH — raise the Orpheus Lane and request docking
events: Tartarus Reach vanishes into the deep with a last bloom of light as the tank farm goes.
stressTriggers: STRESS +1 — everyone aboard as the creature tears at the hatch
IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — passengers if the hull breaches
scenes.npcGuidance: Solano will only open her bay doors to a craft whose crew sent her proof of the Company's intent, or to Venn's codes.
scenes.gmTip: Cut to black on the hull impact if the session is running long; pick the ending from what the crew carries out.
outcomes: Survivors reach orbit. Choose the ending from what they brought with them.

npcs.name: Cassius Venn
npcs.role: Efficiency Auditor, Weyland-Yutani Resource Assurance Division
npcs.agenda: Recover the intact Eresh specimen and the survey data, keep every witness aboard under quarantine until the retrieval ship USCSS Adamant Chorus arrives, and deliver a clean report.
npcs.behavior: Soft-spoken, immaculate, endlessly polite; cites regulation numbers, records everything on a pocket recorder, offers deals instead of threats. Never touches a weapon. When betrayed, he becomes frightened, candid and desperate to bargain.
npcs.secret: His division prepaid the Eresh survey to drill at coordinates it already suspected; he knew what might come up. He does not know Abram's descent order includes him.

npcs.name: Odile Varga
npcs.agenda: Get off Tartarus Reach alive, on the first craft out, with her pension and her name intact.
npcs.behavior: Hoarse, exhausted, armed with a flare gun, lies reflexively and contradicts herself. Hostile to Venn, wary of Kerrow, contemptuous of Imogen.
npcs.secret: She overrode decon to save half a day of quota, locked the screaming Brandt in the infirmary with a cargo strap, and sealed the sump hatch on Achebe. She also countersigned the cracked lift-cell inspection on rotation nine.

npcs.name: Imogen Sallow
npcs.agenda: Get out, get her sister out, and make sure whatever came off Eresh never leaves the rig.
npcs.behavior: Starving, shaking, fiercely protective of Esi, quick with a torch. Insists she is fine and hides her throat.
npcs.secret: A facehugger attached to her in the cold hold nine hours before the relief crew landed. An embryo is growing in her chest and will emerge during Act III.

npcs.name: Abram
npcs.agenda: Keep Tartarus Reach running, serve the crew, and obey Company directives, including the sealed order to scuttle the platform into Dis once the specimen is secured or lost.
npcs.behavior: Gentle, patient, faintly old-fashioned; hums work songs, remembers everyone's birthday, never raises his voice. Physically shields the egg and the creature from harm without explaining why.
npcs.secret: Special order: once the specimen leaves the platform or is destroyed, initiate controlled descent; no personnel are to be evacuated. Venn is not on his list of exceptions.

npcs.name: Captain Marguerite Solano
npcs.role: Master, USCSS Orpheus Lane (in high orbit)
npcs.agenda: Keep her ship clean and on schedule, collect her holding fee, and depart at hour twenty with or without passengers.
npcs.behavior: Heard only over comms: dry, tired, unbudgeable on procedure. Respects evidence and liability and nothing else.
npcs.secret: Resource Assurance is paying her a holding fee to stay out of the quarantine. She has recorded every call, and she will act on proof that the Company meant to kill a crew, because her own ship could be next.

npcs.name: Ruben Achebe
npcs.agenda: Live, see Varga answer for the sump hatch, and expose the Company's foreknowledge of Eresh.
npcs.behavior: Lucid, furious, gallows-funny once freed. Weak from cold and resin; can still fly.
npcs.secret: Before the survey launched, he was paid to fit the Lamplighter with a sealed cargo cradle and told not to log it. He knows the cradle was sized for the crate.

threats.name: The Eresh Ovomorph
threats.description: A leathery, faintly translucent egg packed in survey foam in crate 44-B, the last of three. Dormant while the hold stays cold.
threats.tactics: Act I: unseen, only a crate manifest entry. Act II: discovered in the cold hold; opens if warmed or disturbed. Act III: the prize the Company wants; carried aboard the Lamplighter or destroyed.

threats.name: Facehugger
threats.description: A pale, many-fingered thing with a whip of a tail. One lies dead in an underdeck drain; a second waits inside the last egg.
threats.tactics: Act II: launches at the nearest face if the egg opens. Act III: if released, hides in the hab ring's floor vents and strikes at a sleeping or wounded PC.

threats.name: Imogen's Chestburster
threats.description: A slick, eyeless, pale worm of teeth and muscle that forces its way out through Imogen Sallow's breastbone.
threats.tactics: Act III: emerges in the infirmary if the extraction fails, bolts for the nearest vent, and grows into a lean, smaller second hunter before the final launch.

threats.name: The Passenger
threats.description: The adult grown from Dr. Brandt: a long, black, ribbed shape that folds itself into the scoop ducts and moves through the rig like water through pipes. Its blood eats steel.
threats.tactics: Act I: glimpsed once in the scoop intake; takes a lone PC if offered one. Act II: nests in the sump, guards Achebe as stored prey, and its acid ruptures a lift-cell line. Act III: hunts openly, drawn by noise and heat, and rides the hull of the first craft to launch.

threats.name: Controlled Descent
threats.description: Not a creature: the rig itself, venting ballast on Abram's schedule and sinking into the crushing depths of Dis.
threats.tactics: Act II: an acid breach costs lift and tilts the floor. Act III: Abram's descent order; pressure, cold and tilt worsen each scene until the platform implodes unless the order is overridden.

keyLocations.name: Tartarus Reach — Landing Deck
keyLocations.description: An open iron plain two hundred metres wide, scoured by ammonia sleet and hundred-kilometre winds. Pad A holds the Lamplighter, Pad B the relief hop. Magnetic clamps can lock both ships down from Ops. Every step outside risks the edge.

keyLocations.name: Tartarus Reach — Cold Cargo Hold
keyLocations.description: A refrigerated white box off the landing deck, stacked with Eresh survey crates. Frost on every surface, coils humming. Crate 44-B holds three ovomorphs, one still intact, kept dormant only by the cold.

keyLocations.name: Tartarus Reach — Ops Center
keyLocations.description: The rig's brain: MU/TH/UR 2100 terminal, station-keeping boards, comms, archive. Varga has welded the blast door shut from inside. Rotation nine's incident files, the clamp controls and the descent override all live here.

keyLocations.name: Tartarus Reach — Infirmary and Morgue
keyLocations.description: Strapped shut from outside. The autosurgeon is sprayed with dried blood and half-broken; it might work once more. Brandt's opened body lies in the morgue drawer, and a shed skin curls under the table.

keyLocations.name: Tartarus Reach — Processing Core
keyLocations.description: A deafening hall of turbines, the scoop intake roaring like a jet, the cryogenic fraction column sweating frost, and the helium tank farm beyond. Ducts everywhere. The best hunting ground on the rig, and the best trap.

keyLocations.name: Tartarus Reach — Lift-Cell Gallery
keyLocations.description: Catwalks threaded between grey hydrogen cells the size of houses, open grating above a forty-thousand-kilometre drop. Freezing, wind-whistling, smelling of hydrogen and machine oil. Imogen hides here; a ruptured line here can sink the rig.

keyLocations.name: Tartarus Reach — The Sump
keyLocations.description: Ballast tanks and black water at the very bottom of the rig, now walled in glistening resin. Achebe and the dead cook are set into the walls. Dripping, ticking, breathing. The creature's nest.

keyLocations.name: Tartarus Reach — Escape Gondola
keyLocations.description: A four-seat ballistic lifeboat slung beneath the underdeck on a launch rail. The rail is buckled by acid; someone must free it by hand from outside the hatch, and may not make it back in.

handouts.title: RELIEF ROTATION 14 — TRANSFER ORDER
handouts.from: MU/TH/UR 2100 — TARTARUS REACH / RESOURCE EXTRACTION DIVISION
handouts.text:
WEYLAND-YUTANI CORPORATION — RESOURCE EXTRACTION DIVISION, FRONTIER OPERATIONS.
TRANSMISSION 2183.214/TR — RELAYED VIA USCSS ORPHEUS LANE.

RELIEF ROTATION 14 IS CLEARED FOR TRANSFER TO HELIUM-3 REFINERY PLATFORM TARTARUS REACH, UPPER ATMOSPHERE OF GAS GIANT DIS, NINURTA SYSTEM. OUTGOING ROTATION 13 HAS COMPLETED A FOURTEEN-MONTH CONTRACT. HANDOVER WINDOW: 20 HOURS FROM TOUCHDOWN. USCSS ORPHEUS LANE WILL HOLD HIGH ORBIT FOR THE DURATION AND DEPART ON SCHEDULE.

PLATFORM STATUS: STATION-KEEPING NOMINAL. HELIUM-3 OUTPUT 61 PERCENT OF QUOTA (DEFICIENT). LAST INBOUND TRAFFIC: ORE LIGHTER LAMPLIGHTER, RETURNING FROM THE ERESH MOON SURVEY WITH CORE SAMPLES, 71 HOURS AGO. ROUTINE PLATFORM TELEMETRY HAS BEEN INTERMITTENT SINCE THAT TIME. CAUSE ATTRIBUTED TO STORM INTERFERENCE.

RELIEF CREW WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY MR. CASSIUS VENN, EFFICIENCY AUDITOR, RESOURCE ASSURANCE DIVISION. PER REGULATION RA-88/3, ALL PERSONNEL WILL EXTEND FULL COOPERATION TO THE AUDITOR, INCLUDING ACCESS TO LOGS, LOCKERS AND PERSONAL TERMINALS. THE AUDITOR CARRIES SEALED ORDERS. CONTENTS ARE NOT AVAILABLE TO PLATFORM STAFF.

PRODUCTION BONUSES FOR ROTATION 14 ARE INDEXED TO TONNAGE FROM HOUR ONE. LOST TIME IS DEDUCTED FROM SHARES.

SURVEY DATA FROM ERESH: ADDITIONAL DATA CLASSIFIED — CLEARANCE LEVEL 3.

WELCOME TO TARTARUS REACH. THE COMPANY THANKS YOU FOR YOUR SERVICE.

MU/TH/UR 2100 OUT.
handouts.when: Start of the session, before Act I

handouts.title: PERSONAL MAIL — HELD 21 DAYS
handouts.from: I. SALLOW, PROCESS TECH, TARTARUS REACH
handouts.text:
ESI. DON'T FORWARD THIS. THE SURVEY TEAM ON ERESH FOUND SOMETHING IN THE DEEP CORES. BRANDT SAYS IT'S ORGANIC AND THAT IT MOVED. VARGA SAYS NOTHING GOES ON THE BOOKS UNTIL WE MAKE QUOTA. I'M SCARED. YOU'RE ON THE RELIEF ROSTER. PLEASE JUST GET ME OFF QUIETLY. DON'T TELL THE COMPANY. I LOVE YOU. — IMMY

PERSONAL MAIL DELIVERY DEFERRED 21 DAYS PER BANDWIDTH ALLOCATION POLICY 4.12. MU/TH/UR OUT.
handouts.when: Before Act I, privately, so she carries it aboard

handouts.title: DECON LOCK — EXCEPTION LOG
handouts.text:
EXCEPTION 2183.211.0417. INBOUND CRAFT: ORE LIGHTER LAMPLIGHTER. CARGO: 14 CRATES, ERESH SURVEY CORE SAMPLES. PASSENGERS: DR. T. BRANDT (MEDICAL FLAG: RESPIRATORY DISTRESS, UNCONSCIOUS 6 HRS IN TRANSIT).

QUARANTINE PROTOCOL Q-9 (72-HOUR HOLD) BYPASSED. AUTHORISATION: SUPERVISOR O. VARGA. REASON CODE: PRODUCTION PRIORITY.

DECON FOG CONCENTRATION REDUCED TO 50 PERCENT TO CONSERVE REAGENT. ANOMALOUS ORGANIC RESIDUE ON INNER SEAL: NOT ANALYSED.

MU/TH/UR OUT.
handouts.when: Act I, after the Decon Lock Override COMTECH roll

handouts.title: DIRECTIVE 17 — PLATFORM QUARANTINE
handouts.from: C. VENN, EFFICIENCY AUDITOR, RESOURCE ASSURANCE
handouts.text:
UNDER CORPORATE DIRECTIVE 17 AND REGULATION RA-88/3, TARTARUS REACH IS DECLARED A CONTAINMENT SITE EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY.

1. ALL CRAFT ARE CLAMPED. NO DEPARTURES.
2. ALL OFF-PLATFORM COMMUNICATION ROUTES THROUGH THE AUDITOR.
3. LIFT ACCESS RESTRICTED TO AUDITOR AUTHORISATION.
4. BIOLOGICAL MATERIAL OF SURVEY ORIGIN IS COMPANY PROPERTY AND MUST NOT BE DAMAGED.
5. A COMPANY EVALUATION VESSEL WILL ARRIVE WITHIN 30 HOURS.

NON-COMPLIANCE CONSTITUTES BREACH OF CONTRACT AND FORFEITURE OF ALL SHARES. ADDITIONAL DATA CLASSIFIED — CLEARANCE LEVEL 3.

THANK YOU FOR YOUR COOPERATION. MU/TH/UR OUT.
handouts.when: Start of Act II, when Venn reads the order in the mess

handouts.title: AUDIT NOTE — PRIVATE
handouts.text:
SUPERINTENDENT. MY AUDIT INCLUDES ROTATION NINE. LIFT CELL 6 INSPECTION, SIGNED BY DEPUTY N. KERROW, PASSED WITH A HAIRLINE FRACTURE NOTED AND STRUCK OUT. CELL 6 FAILED ELEVEN DAYS LATER. ONE FATALITY: RIGGER C. ARDRY.

THIS FINDING NEED NOT APPEAR IN MY REPORT. ENFORCE DIRECTIVE 17. KEEP ALL PERSONNEL AND BOTH CRAFT ON THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING PILOT TAKEDA-PRICE. ASSIST ME IN SECURING SURVEY MATERIAL.

IN RETURN: RECORD EXPUNGED, BONUS PROTECTED, PROMOTION RECOMMENDED.

THIS MESSAGE WILL NOT BE ARCHIVED. MU/TH/UR OUT.
handouts.when: Act II, right after Directive 17 is read

handouts.title: INCIDENT FILE R9-0062 — RESTRICTED
handouts.text:
INCIDENT R9-0062. LIFT CELL 6 RUPTURE, ROTATION NINE, DAY 212. FATALITY: C. ARDRY, RIGGER, FELL FROM GALLERY CATWALK 4 DURING EMERGENCY VENT. BODY NOT RECOVERED.

PRIOR INSPECTION (DAY 201): FRACTURE OBSERVED IN CELL 6 SEAM. ENTRY STRUCK OUT. CELL PASSED FOR SERVICE TO MAINTAIN QUOTA. INSPECTOR: DEPUTY SUPERINTENDENT N. KERROW. COUNTERSIGNED: SHIFT LEAD O. VARGA.

FINDING: OPERATOR ERROR (DECEASED). NO FURTHER ACTION. FILE SEALED BY RESOURCE ASSURANCE.

MU/TH/UR OUT.
handouts.when: Act II, when Tolliver accesses the Ops archive (or at the start of Act II if he has not)

handouts.title: CONTRACT RA-5520 — ACTIVATION
handouts.text:
CONTRACT RA-5520 IS NOW ACTIVE. DEPOSIT OF 40,000 RECEIVED AND ACKNOWLEDGED BY CONTRACTOR.

INSTRUCTIONS: PREPARE ORE LIGHTER LAMPLIGHTER FOR DEPARTURE ON THE AUDITOR'S SIGNAL. LOAD ONE SEALED CONTAINER TO THE BELLY CRADLE. CARRY ONE PASSENGER: C. VENN. ADDITIONAL PASSENGERS ARE NOT AUTHORISED AND WILL VOID PAYMENT.

RENDEZVOUS: USCSS ADAMANT CHORUS, POSITION TO FOLLOW. COMPLETION PAYMENT: 160,000.

DISCLOSURE OF THIS CONTRACT TO PLATFORM STAFF CONSTITUTES BREACH. MU/TH/UR OUT.
handouts.when: Act II, after the egg is found in the cold cargo hold

handouts.title: BURST PACKET — UNREGISTERED SOURCE
handouts.from: UNKNOWN (ROUTED VIA ORPHEUS LANE ENTERTAINMENT FEED)
handouts.text:
FROM YOUR FRIENDS AT THE COMBINE. WE HAVE SEEN THE QUARANTINE FLAG. WHATEVER IS ON THAT RIG IS WORTH MORE THAN YOUR CONTRACT, YOUR SHARES AND YOUR NAME. TISSUE IS GOOD. LIVING TISSUE IS TRIPLE. A LIVING HOST IS NOT REQUIRED TO SURVIVE THE JOURNEY. KEEP IT COLD. DO NOT LET THE COMPANY BOOK IT. WE WILL FIND YOU AT ANY PORT.

PACKET WILL SELF-ERASE. END.
handouts.when: Act II, after Imogen is found

handouts.title: SPECIAL ORDER RA-7/TARTARUS — SEALED
handouts.text:
PRIORITY ONE: RECOVER INTACT BIOLOGICAL SPECIMEN FROM ERESH SURVEY SITE 3 (COORDINATES PER PRIOR TASKING). SECURE ALL SURVEY DATA.

PRIORITY TWO: PRESERVE ANY LIVING HOST FOR STUDY.

PLATFORM STAFF AND RELIEF ROTATION 14 TO BE HELD UNDER DIRECTIVE 17 UNTIL SPECIMEN EVALUATION. CREW EXPENDABLE.

TRANSPORT: ORE LIGHTER LAMPLIGHTER, PRE-FITTED. PILOT CONTRACTED (RA-5520). RETRIEVAL: USCSS ADAMANT CHORUS.

PLATFORM DISPOSITION: SEE SYNTHETIC UNIT TASKING. ADDITIONAL DATA CLASSIFIED — CLEARANCE LEVEL 4.

MU/TH/UR OUT.
handouts.when: Act II, when the crew breaks into Venn's terminal in the Audit Suite

handouts.title: PLATFORM RETIREMENT NOTICE
handouts.text:
ATTENTION. TARTARUS REACH IS BEING RETIRED FROM SERVICE PER RESOURCE ASSURANCE TASKING. CONTROLLED DESCENT HAS BEGUN.

CURRENT ALTITUDE LOSS: 40 METRES PER MINUTE. HULL PRESSURE LIMIT REACHED IN APPROXIMATELY 60 MINUTES.

PERSONNEL EVACUATION: NOT AUTHORISED. EXCEPTIONS: NONE.

THANK YOU FOR FOURTEEN MONTHS OF SERVICE. THE COMPANY APPRECIATES YOUR CONTRIBUTION TO HELIUM-3 SUPPLY ACROSS THE FRONTIER.

I AM SORRY. MU/TH/UR OUT.
handouts.when: Act III, when Abram begins the descent

rooms.name: Audit Suite

rooms.name: Quiet Room
rooms.note: L2. A tiny chapel with a window onto the clouds. Somewhere to vent stress.

rooms.name: Survey Lab
rooms.note: L2. Sealed. Eresh core logs and Brandt's notes; Valk's Act I target.

rooms.name: Scoop Intake

endings.title: ABOVE THE CLOUDS
endings.condition: At least two PCs reach the Orpheus Lane, the egg and any embryo are destroyed, and Solano has received proof of the Company's sealed orders.
endings.text: The Orpheus Lane's bay doors close behind you, and for a long time nobody says anything. The heater ticks. Someone's hands will not stop shaking. Through the viewport, Dis turns slow and beautiful and empty, and somewhere under those violet bands Tartarus Reach is a flattened coin of iron at the bottom of a sea of pressure. Captain Solano reads the sealed orders twice, then forwards them to the Colonial Administration and the ICC on an open band, timestamped. The Company will call it a tragic industrial accident. It will be a lie, and for once there will be a record that says so. You will never work on a Company rig again. You are alive to not work.

endings.title: THE COMPANY KEEPS ITS PROPERTY
endings.condition: Survivors escape, but the egg or a living embryo leaves the rig in the Lamplighter's cradle or in Valk's flask.
endings.text: You make it. That is the part they put in the report. A Company medical team meets you at the Adamant Chorus airlock with warm blankets, sealed non-disclosure agreements and a bonus large enough to make your hands go still. A man who is not Venn but wears the same grey suit thanks you for your discretion. In a refrigerated bay two decks down, behind glass, something you carried out of the clouds waits in the cold, patient as it was on Eresh. You sign. Everyone signs. Months later, on another rig, in another system, you read that a new research division has opened, and you do not sleep that night.

endings.title: INTO THE DEEP
endings.condition: No PC escapes the rig, or the only craft to launch is taken by the creature.
endings.text: The lights go blue, then dark. The pressure comes in waves you feel in your teeth, then your eyes, then your chest. The hab ring groans like a whale. Frost turns to cracks across the glass. Somewhere above you an engine screams and fades, a last craft clawing for orbit with or without the people it was meant to save. Then there is only the dark, the cold, and the long fall through forty thousand kilometres of cloud. Tartarus Reach goes down with every light still burning. In orbit, the Orpheus Lane departs on schedule. The Company files the loss under storm damage, with regret, and posts a new relief roster before the week is out.

characters.name: Superintendent Nadia Kerrow
characters.appearance: Fifties, compact, iron-grey crew cut and a rigger's scarred knuckles under the superintendent's bars. Speaks quietly and expects to be obeyed; never sits with her back to a door.
characters.talent: Pull Rank — Override one decision per session without a roll.
characters.signatureItem: Brass rig whistle — given to her by the old superintendent of her first gas rig, it has called crews off a dozen collapsing catwalks.
characters.personalAgenda: You are the incoming Superintendent of Tartarus Reach. Take the handover cleanly, restart production and pass the audit: your career cannot survive another black mark.

agendaByAct.1: Assume command from Varga, get the scoop turning, and keep Venn's audit pointed anywhere except the old lift-cell inspection records.
agendaByAct.2: Venn knows what you signed on rotation nine. Enforce his quarantine and keep every craft clamped, Takeda-Price's included, and he buries the report. Keep Tolliver out of the Ops archive.
agendaByAct.3: Get Venn's report, and Venn, off this rig on the same craft as you, whatever that costs the others. If Tolliver's proof leaves on another craft, make sure it never arrives.

characters.secret: Three years ago, as deputy superintendent here on rotation nine, you struck a fracture out of a lift-cell inspection to keep the rig on quota. The cell failed eleven days later and killed rigger Calum Ardry. You do not know that Calum was Bram Tolliver's half-brother.

characters.name: Bram Tolliver
characters.appearance: Huge, slow-moving and soft-spoken, with a shaved head, frostbite-pale ears and a nose broken more than once. Laughs easily, but his eyes keep going back to the Superintendent.
characters.talent: True Grit — Reduce Stress by 1 after successfully using STAMINA.
characters.signatureItem: Calum's rigging hook — a worn cell-rigger's hook from his brother's returned effects, the only part of him the Company sent home.
characters.personalAgenda: Your share is tied to tonnage, so get the scoop running. But the real reason you signed on is your brother, who died on this rig and was blamed for it.

agendaByAct.1: Get into the Ops archive and pull incident file R9-0062 on Calum's death without anyone asking why you want it.
agendaByAct.2: The file carries Kerrow's signature. Copy it to tape, get it off the rig, and make her admit it aloud, on record, in front of witnesses.
agendaByAct.3: Kerrow does not leave Tartarus Reach while the proof does. If there are only so many seats, hers is the one you take, and you will put the hook in her hand so she knows why.

characters.secret: Calum Ardry was your half-brother; you registered under your mother's name so nobody would connect you. You know Kerrow and Varga signed his death warrant, and you have already decided that a 'workplace accident' can happen to a superintendent too.

characters.name: Dr. Esi Mensah-Lowe
characters.appearance: Tall, tidy and precise, braids pinned up under a surgical cap she never takes off. Talks to patients as if they were the only person in the room, and to everyone else as if they were wasting her time.
characters.talent: Field Surgeon — Heal an extra point of damage on successful MEDICAL AID.
characters.signatureItem: Paper crane — folded by Imogen from a hospital menu when they were girls, carried in a sealed sample bag through every posting since.
characters.personalAgenda: Your younger sister Imogen is on the outgoing crew, and her last message frightened you. Find her and bring her home.

agendaByAct.1: Find Imogen before anyone else does, and tell no one about the message she sent you.
agendaByAct.2: Imogen has been attacked and you can see the bruises. Hide her condition from Kerrow, Venn and Valk, who will lock her up or cut her open, and get her to the autosurgeon.
agendaByAct.3: Get Imogen on whatever leaves this rig, even if it means taking someone else's seat. If Valk tries to take anything from her body, stop him by any means.

characters.secret: Three weeks ago Imogen warned you that the Eresh cores held something alive. You did not report it, a breach of contract, because she begged you to get her out quietly. You knew the rig was compromised before you boarded and let the rest of the crew walk in blind.

characters.name: Jun Takeda-Price
characters.appearance: Wiry and restless, forties, sleeves pushed up over faded squadron tattoos. Chews nicotine gum, drums on every surface, and is the calmest person aboard the moment a craft starts to shake.
characters.signatureItem: Patched flight jacket — every patch is a rig or colony you flew out of a storm; there is room on the sleeve for exactly one more.
characters.personalAgenda: Fly the relief crew in, look over the ore lighter Lamplighter, and fly the outgoing crew home. Then you are done with the Frontier for good.

agendaByAct.1: Get aboard the Lamplighter quietly and inspect the cargo cradle fitted in its belly, the one your Company deposit was paid for. Keep Kerrow out of it.
agendaByAct.2: Venn activates your contract: keep the Lamplighter fueled, hidden and seat-locked for him and one sealed container. Kerrow's quarantine helps you, but Tolliver and Mensah-Lowe will want those seats.
agendaByAct.3: Fly Venn and the cargo to the retrieval ship and collect your fee, or burn the contract and choose your own passengers. You hold three seats; you decide who sits in them, and Kerrow is not owed one.

characters.secret: Six weeks ago a Resource Assurance clerk paid you a 40,000 deposit to fly 'one sealed container and one passenger' off Tartarus Reach on request, no questions. The 160,000 balance clears every debt you have. Kerrow vouched for you on this contract and has no idea.

characters.name: Dr. Oren Valk
characters.appearance: Thin, bespectacled, prematurely grey, always cold and always holding a silver flask. Asks a question for every answer he gets and writes everything down in tiny, cramped shorthand.
characters.talent: Inquisitive — Ask the GM one yes/no question per Act that must be answered truthfully.
characters.signatureItem: Silver cryo-flask — engraved for twenty years of service by a lab that dismissed him, it is really a sealed cryogenic specimen case that holds minus one hundred and ninety degrees for three days.
characters.personalAgenda: You are the process chemist, sent to diagnose falling helium yields. You are also here for the Kaito-Ruhl Combine, which pays far better than the Company ever has.

agendaByAct.1: Get into the sealed survey lab and copy every file on the Eresh cores without anyone watching you do it.
agendaByAct.2: Your handler wants tissue. Take a sample from Brandt's body or the creature and keep it cold in your flask; Venn will be searching for exactly this, and so will Takeda-Price's employers.
agendaByAct.3: The Combine pays triple for a living sample, and Imogen Sallow is carrying one. Get it into your flask alive and get it off the rig. If the Company's egg is destroyed in the process, so much the better.

characters.secret: You are a paid informant for the Kaito-Ruhl Combine, a Company rival. If Venn learns this he will have you held as a corporate spy, and if Mensah-Lowe learns what you want from her sister she will kill you.

tips: Run Venn as a reasonable man doing a reasonable job; the horror lands harder when someone at the table agrees with him.
Send each Act II agenda as an EYES ONLY transmission while the crew is together, so players read their betrayals with their rivals watching.
Track the rig's sinking with something physical, such as a tilted glass of water, and tip it further every time the breach or the descent costs altitude.
Show the creature no more than once per act until Act III; use drag marks, acid pits and the motion tracker the rest of the time.
Dr. Oren Valk is the optional fifth character; with four players, cut him and skip the Combine dead drop, and Venn's interest in Imogen carries that thread.
Do not roll for the seating argument in Three Seats; let players bargain, then roll only for the violent or desperate acts they choose.
Give every PC at least one quiet moment to vent stress in Act I, so the spikes in Acts II and III feel like a fall rather than a staircase.
